name: Petstore — REST basics
description: CRUD endpoints showing URL, path-template, query, header and JSON body matching, priorities and status codes.

name: Echo server — see what you send
description: Every method and path answers with JSON describing the request: method, path, query, headers, body and parsed JSON or form fields. Point a client at it to see exactly what it sends.

name: Fake data — realistic test data
description: Names, e-mails, addresses, products, prices and dates that change on every call. Lists built with a loop and data in other languages.

name: Dynamic responses — templating
description: Responses built from the request with Handlebars: echo path, query, headers and JSON body, random data, dates and conditionals.

name: Matching patterns — from real projects
description: The patterns teams use most in real WireMock setups: magic test ids for errors, JSONPath filters and regex on body fields, priority fallbacks, one stub for every environment, proxying chosen ids to a real service, transformer parameters and content negotiation.

name: Orders — CRUD with saved data
description: A full REST resource from one stub: list, filter, create, update and delete orders. Records are saved, survive restarts and can be edited in the Data tab.

name: Shopping cart — stateful scenarios
description: A cart that changes state across calls using WireMock scenarios: empty → item added → checked out.

name: Payments — webhooks and callbacks
description: Answer at once and call back later, forward a request to a partner, or wait for a partner and answer with its response. Every callout shows up in the Callouts tab, and a catch-all receiver catches any webhook.

name: Resilience testing — faults & delays
description: Slow responses, random latency, dropped connections, 429/503 with Retry-After, a stub that fails 1 call in 5 and a maintenance switch you turn on and off. Test your timeouts and retries.

name: Bookshop — from an OpenAPI file
description: Stubs generated from an OpenAPI spec, plus hand-written error cases and response files: a CSV price list and a cover image.

name: Calculator — SOAP from WSDL
description: Generated from a WSDL: one stub per operation, the ?wsdl endpoint and a fault for unknown operations. Plus a hand-written stub matching on XPath values.

name: Library — GraphQL from a schema
description: Imported from SDL: one endpoint answers every query and mutation with data that follows the schema, plus fixed answers for a missing book and a conflicting loan. Try it in the GraphQL console.

name: Inventory — gRPC from a descriptor set
description: A StockService with unary, server-streaming and client-streaming methods. Matches on the request message and on metadata, answers with templated messages or gRPC statuses, and works with grpcurl through server reflection.

name: GitHub REST API — sandbox (unofficial)
description: Users, repositories, issues, comments, pull requests and commits from GitHub's published OpenAPI description (github/rest-api-description, MIT), answered with GitHub's own examples. Point a client at it instead of api.github.com.

name: Stripe API — sandbox (unofficial)
description: Customers, payment intents, charges, refunds and balance from Stripe's published OpenAPI spec (stripe/openapi, MIT). Answers follow Stripe's schemas, filled with generated values. Point a client at it instead of api.stripe.com.

name: Twilio Messaging and Voice API — sandbox (unofficial)
description: Send and read SMS messages and calls from Twilio's published OpenAPI spec (twilio/twilio-oai, MIT), answered with Twilio's own examples. Point a client at it instead of api.twilio.com.

name: UPS Tracking, Rating and Address API — sandbox (unofficial)
description: Track a package, rate a shipment, validate an address and get transit times from UPS's published OpenAPI specs (UPS-API/api-documentation, MIT). Answers follow UPS's schemas, with its examples where it has them and generated values elsewhere. Point a client at it instead of onlinetools.ups.com/api.

name: Amadeus flight booking API — sandbox (unofficial)
description: Search airports and cities, search and price flight offers, and create, read and cancel a flight order from Amadeus's published Self-Service specs (amadeus4dev/amadeus-open-api-specification, MIT), answered with Amadeus's own examples. Point a client at it instead of test.api.amadeus.com.
